summary: Allocates a 24-byte node via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper, initializes it as a sound-buffer node via SoundBufferAllocator(node, 1024, a2), then appends it to the singly-advanced list whose head is tracked at this+0x2C. When the list is empty the new node becomes this+0x2C with its backward slot cleared; otherwise the forward-pointer chain at node+0x14 is walked to the end and the new node is linked with its backward slot pointing at the previous last node. Returns the new node pointer, or 0 if allocation failed.

local_names.result: initialized node returned by SoundBufferAllocator (0 when allocation failed)
local_names.v5: current list tail during the forward walk, starts at this+0x2C
local_names.i: next node during the forward walk, advanced via the +0x14 slot

operations.description: Allocate a 24-byte block for a new list node via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper.
If the allocation returned 0, set result to 0 and skip initialization.
Initialize the allocated block as a sound-buffer node: result = SoundBufferAllocator(node, 1024, a2).
Load v5 = this[11] (offset 0x2C); if it is non-NULL the list is non-empty and the append walks the chain.
Walk the forward-pointer chain: start at v5 and advance v5 = i while i = *(v5 + 20) is non-NULL, i.e. follow the +0x14 slot of each node to reach the last one.
Link the new node at the end of the non-empty list: set the previous last node's +0x14 slot to result and result[4] (offset +0x10) back to that previous node.
Empty-list branch: set this[11] (offset 0x2C) to result and clear result[4] (offset +0x10) to 0; the new node is the only node.
Return result, the new node pointer (or 0 on allocation failure).
Called by sub_546450 (00546450) and sub_546AA0 (00546aa0) to append sound-buffer nodes.

unresolved: The packet field list includes this+0x40 as a read, but the raw source walks from this+0x2C via each node's +0x14 slot and never reads this+0x40; the relationship between the two list anchors is unresolved.
The new node's backward slot at +0x10 is written but has no packet field evidence; its exact meaning depends on the sound-buffer list layout.
Whether the list is doubly linked (a backward slot exists at +0x10) or the +0x10 value is used for another purpose depends on SoundBufferAllocator and the list consumers.
